hypotheses.claim: ClayCode canonicalization must be type-directed so Set fields normalize order/duplicates while Ordered/list/role semantics preserve order.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One schema-blind structural canonicalizer is sufficient for all collections.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production typed IR proves all order-sensitive fields are separately represented before hashing and schema-blind canonicalization cannot collapse distinct executable/replay behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Equivalent declared-infix and generic relation surfaces can share semantic_hash while retaining distinct contract_hash/provenance instances.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Surface form must be part of executable semantic identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched production parser/IR shows equivalent surfaces lower to meaningfully different typed IR, effect traces or replay requiring semantic identity separation.

hypotheses.claim: Stable generated artifact identity should exclude per-run capability instances; runtime authority should bind through distinct deployment/execution receipt identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production build/replay shows embedding per-run authority improves security/correctness without harming reproducibility, cacheability or differential validation.

negative_results.claim: Schema-blind sorting/deduplicating all collection-like syntax is unsafe for ClayCode semantic hashing.
negative_results.evidence: Blind canonicalizer hash-collided forward and reversed external_effect lifecycle; typed Ordered canonicalizer distinguished them.

negative_results.claim: Embedding per-run capability identity in generated code contaminates stable artifact identity.
negative_results.evidence: Concurrent HTTP v1 produced different fresh target hashes; run-local 10,000-token discriminator produced 10,000 embedded-token artifact hashes versus one runtime-handle artifact hash and 10,000 deployment hashes.
